questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the teaching language was english. It was also crucial for me to be in a german-speaking country because i wanted to improve my german.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Switzerland was very expensive and the prices of everything hindered me in a lot of ways. I have never been so economically stressed or felt so poor as I did in Switzerland. Not being able to have a job in Switzerland (as I have in Copenhagen) only worsened this. If i had been richer it would have been a 9/10.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, although in Lucerne you had to fill in a lot of physical paperwork which I am not used to doing in Denmark.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recieved all of the information needed to register and study there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived at the student mentor foundation Lucerne at Eichhof. I got a room thorugh the uni, but i had to be quick to apply for it. Some of the others were too slow and had to live someplace else and pay a higher rent.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is a good idea to buy a bicycle.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The landlord (SMFL) is very stringent and annoyed at ANY noises after 22:00. Even on a friday. They are also very stringent about the cleaning and so far (2 months after moving out) none of my friends or me have recieved our security deposit back. I would strongly advice anyone to be vary of this when choosing accomodation. The rooms  and dorms themselves very decent new build quality.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registered by logging in with my Studnet account and I followed all the classes which made the most sense for me. It was very straight forward and easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I didnt need any help, but i know that the interantional office wanted to help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got every single class that I wanted, and as far as I know everyone got the classes they wished for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be sure that your exam dates are decent. I had 6 exams in 2 weeks and I wish i had taken some exams at a later date so it wouldn't be so cramped.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I felt like the oral exams being made in groups of 2 was a weird concept and I didnt like that.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The law courses tought in english are all 5 ECTS and pretty good. The difficulty levels vary a lot. Some were much easier then UCPH, and some very about the same difficulty as UCPH. Most courses were slightly easier because we didnt have to read as much as I am used to. The grades were also very neat and I havent heard of anyone failing.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was similar to seminarundervisning at UCPH. With small classes of 10-40 students and a lot of discussions. There was no written homework. Only a lot of reading material.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
European Economic law
International Arbitration
International Enviromental law
International law of contemproary media
Introduction to swiss law
Law and society in a global context

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can recpmmend introduction to swiss law because it is made for exchange students and gives a good overview of swiss law. I can also recommend enviromental law if you are interested in that kind of thing, the professor is very passionate and sweet.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to pay for a residents permit on arrival which cost about 1200 kroner. That was a bummer.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: EVERYTHING is expensive in Switzerland! The only things that I found cheap were some itens in the supermarket and transportation if you had the half fare youth card. I cooked a lot for myself because of this.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UNILU has a nice free gym which i used almost every day.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A few parties and a lot of sports clubs. I didnt participate in thoose sports clubs, but I know that some of the other students did with great succes.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking! Switzerland is a hikers paradise and it is one of the few things which is free.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking and skiing. Me and a few other exchange students went on at least 1 big hike every week. It was wonderful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. I speak german fluently, so that helped a lot.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to learn Swiss German

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Swiss are very strict. I had a hard time with this at first.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I liked the outdoorsy vibe. It was very normal for everyone to go hiking, skiing, running or sailing on the weekends.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Have enough money
Bring good outdoorsy clothes
Buy a cheap bicycle for commuting. there is an auction called "velobörse" 2 times a year for this.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people from arouund the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I felt lonely at times and missed my girlfriend, friends and family a lot.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: DO IT! Besides the financial struggles Lucerne was a perfect destination for me and it almost felt like a holiday being there :)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
